rows.evidence: Q1: Conditions, materials and methods / Results and Discussion - three-year (2013-2015) replicated field experiments at KazNIIZiR demonstration plots on sugar beet comparing furrow irrigation, surface and subsurface drip with and without mulch film, with weed counts, biomass, yield (Tables 2-4) and economic calculations.
rows.notes: The 8-10 fold weed reduction in the passage is attributed by the study to the mulch film, not to drip irrigation: weed counts were 18-23 plants/m2 in options with mulch film versus up to 165 plants/m2 in options without mulch film (which include the drip options without film), and the Conclusion states that sugar beet cultivation under the mulch film at drip irrigation reduces weed infestation 8-10 times compared to the control. No drip-without-mulch versus furrow weed comparison is reported separately; drip options without film required the same three-stage herbicide programme as the control. The evidence is therefore about plastic mulch under drip, not about drip itself, so Q2 is 'no'. Also no replication statistics, dispersion measures or stated limitations for the weed result.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a short field-trial report with little statistical detail; weed data are reported as ranges without treatment-by-treatment breakdown or dispersion.
